studies.Population: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer (PLCO) Screening study participants
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Association of dietary tomato intake with bladder cancer risk in a prospective cohort of 101,683 individuals with 12.5 years of follow-up.
studies.Authors: Xu X, Xie B, Li S, Wang S, Xia D, Meng H
studies.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quintile of raw tomato intake (Q5 vs Q1)

sample_size.excerpt: Association of dietary tomato intake with bladder cancer risk in a prospective cohort of 101,683 individuals with 12.5 years of follow-up.

cases.excerpt: After a median of 12.5 years of follow-up, 774 incident bladder cancer cases were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: We found no statistically significant association between dietary intake of raw tomatoes and bladder cancer risk (Adjusted model: HRQ5 VS Q1 = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.95-1.52; P for trend = 0.243).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found no statistically significant association between dietary intake of raw tomatoes and bladder cancer risk (Adjusted model: HRQ5 VS Q1 = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.95-1.52; P for trend = 0.243).
